text:
alex: heads-up — after merging PR 9150 into main we started seeing allocation jitter on the longseq perf harness. canary CPU and mem oscillating during steady-state runs. attaching a short summary below, asking for quick eyes.

jamie: can you paste the bench link + exact test config?

alex: bench run: https://bench.redwood/internal/runs/9150-noise, config: longseq-8k, concurrency=32, steady-window=6m. observed p95 latency increase and allocator churn.

ravi: quick question — is this the alloc path change from the allocator refactor in 9150 or the new batching heuristic?

alex: looks like allocator refactor. the change to slab-return timing seems correlated. we did an A/B locally toggling the refactor flag and noise drops.

emily: do we have flamegraphs or heap profiles from the canary pods? if not, can we add now and replay?

alex: i grabbed one heap profile and a brief perf trace. snippet from the trace: 
```
alloc_retire_slow_path +34% samples
kv_cache_prefetch (idle) spikes aligned with GC windows
context-switches increased by ~12%
```

alex: full artifacts: gs://redwood-artifacts/bench/4791234567/{heap.pb.gz,perf.trace,bench-summary.json}

ops-bot: canary: deploy pr-9150 -> canary-alloc-1 started

ops-bot: canary: observed mem jitter; automated canary rollback triggered at step 4

jamie: ok please mark the PR as hold. @ravi @emily can you do a quick look at the allocator change? low-risk revert option might be to reintroduce the previous slab return cadence.

ravi: will take a look this afternoon. initial read: race window on free-list return could cause temporary backpressure leading to allocator stalls under multi-worker load.

emily: i can repro locally with longseq-8k + concurrency 24. i’ll push a tiny patch that toggles the timing to previous cadence, run bench, and post numbers.

emily: quick perf numbers after toggle (local): p95 1.12s -> 0.98s, p99 1.9s -> 1.6s, alloc churn down 38%.

alex: great — if that holds in CI we can either patch or add a feature-flag and keep the refactor behind it until we address the edge-case.

sre-oncall: FYI if this affects customer-facing clusters we should open an incident and run targeted canaries in eu-west1 as well. i can spin those up.

jamie: thanks all. next steps: @emily run CI bench on the toggle and post results, @ravi prepare a short PR with a reversible toggle, @alex hold merge and add a note on the PR describing the regression and rationale. i’ll follow up with a short postmortem note if we need it. :thumbsup:
